source: Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) Bureau of Forest Fire Control and Forestry: Legacy Tree Program and Champion Trees list
endpoint: https://www.mass.gov/doc/massachusetts-legacy-tree-list-0/download (Legacy Trees 2026, xlsx, 476 rows) and https://www.mass.gov/doc/champion-trees/download (Champion Trees 2026, xlsx, 139 rows, the top-ranked subset per species), both linked from https://www.mass.gov/guides/massachusetts-legacy-tree-program
licence: Massachusetts public record, per Mass.gov Terms of Use (genuinely two-tier, read in full, not a named open licence like CC BY)
licence_proof: https://www.mass.gov/massgov-terms-of-use, section 'Public records and copyright', quoted verbatim: "All of the material posted on the Commonwealth's websites and available to the public without use of an authenticating and authorizing mechanism (such as a 'PIN' or password) is public record. Most of the public record posted on Commonwealth websites can be copied and used for any purpose. For example, all judicial opinions and all laws and regulations are public record." The SAME page also states the Commonwealth holds copyright in 'most of the content on Mass.gov' (design, layout, prose) and restricts THAT to fair use. This dataset is raw factual survey data (species, address, county, measurements) compiled by state foresters under a public program, not editorial content, design or layout, so it falls on the public-record side of the page's own distinction, matching this project's 'US federal/state public domain' licence category. Recorded honestly as the two-tier reading it is, same discipline as the Castilla y Leon IGCYL-NC case: the licence NAME is not a clean CC tag, but the terms as read do permit commercial-leaning reuse of the data itself.
designation: Two related but distinct lists from the same DCR program: 'Champion Trees' (139 rows, the single largest known specimen of each species statewide, nominated and field-verified by DCR foresters, feeding the National Champion Tree Program register) and 'Legacy Trees' (476 rows, a broader ranked list per species including runners-up, e.g. the state's 2nd, 3rd, 6th largest of a species). Both are real designations, verified in person by a trained forester per the program's own description, not a bulk street-tree inventory.
attribution: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR), Bureau of Forest Fire Control and Forestry
scope: All rows from both files. 'location' is a free-text address or landmark name (e.g. '28 Moreland St', 'Mount Auburn Cemetery'), never a coordinate: this register needs geocoding before any pin ships, and the field is sometimes null (measured but the address is not made public in the sheet, e.g. private-land trees under 'Location (if Publicly Available)').
vitality_field: None. No survey-date-implies-alive field either beyond 'Date Measured', which for some rows runs back to the 2010s. Alive-now stays a per-tree check, same as every register scanned so far.
coordinate_note: No coordinates in either file, only city/county and a free-text location string. Semantic filter passes (both are genuine per-species designations), but this is a lead list requiring geocoding per hard rule 10 and per-tree verification of public access, same tier as Nara's town-level list.

cities_of_interest.note: Mount Auburn Cemetery (Watertown/Cambridge border, ~4 km from downtown Boston, an existing tourist destination with its own visitor infrastructure) alone accounts for roughly 25 of the 83 Greater Boston legacy rows across many species, the single densest cluster in the whole file and a strong candidate walkable cluster for deepening Boston's page or a Cambridge page.
